{"command":"cat > dev/lab/targets.yml <<'EOF'
# Deliberately outdated servers for the first OpenVAS scan. They join the
# appliance stack's network and publish no host ports, so nothing outside
# Docker can reach them.
#
#   docker compose -f dev/lab/targets.yml up -d
#   docker compose -f dev/lab/targets.yml down
name: scanner-lab

services:
  httpd:
    image: httpd:2.4.49
    # CVE-2021-41773 is only reachable with "Require all granted" on the
    # filesystem root, so the first occurrence in httpd.conf is flipped.
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sed -i '0,/Require all denied/s//Require all granted/' /usr/local/apache2/conf/httpd.conf && exec httpd-foreground"]
  tomcat:
    image: tomcat:9.0.30
    # Some builds of this image ship the default webapps in webapps.dist.
    command: ["sh", "-c", "[ -d webapps.dist ] && cp -rn webapps.dist/. webapps/; exec catalina.sh run"]
  redis:
    image: redis:5.0.7
  nginx:
    image: nginx:1.16.1

networks:
  default:
    name: scanner-appliance_default
    external: true
EOF

---

The first end-to-end scans with the real feed ran on 2026-10-05 in the container lab (see [[local-dev-environment]]). They work, and they exposed defects the scripted fakes could not, because the fakes encode assumptions about the engine that turned out wrong.

**Fixed on 2026-10-05, in the working tree, not committed by me:**
- Product inventory. ospd-openvas sends host details as `Log Message` results on the pseudo port `general/Host_Details`, not as the `Host Detail` type, and consolidated detection tests report on `general/tcp` with the port in a `Location:` line. `daemon/internal/engine/normalize.go` now handles both, so ports get product, version and CPE, and hosts get an OS guess.
- Slow test descriptions. `nvt.Cache.Lookup` now fetches 8 or more misses in one streamed pass (`osp.Client.GetVTs`), about 34 s for the whole feed against 4.7 s per single lookup. A cold 4-host scan went from 805 s to 380 s.

**Open, verified, not fixed:**
- Inventory mode sees no services with the real engine. Its scan config has no "Port scanners" family and the engine default is `unscanned_closed = yes`, so every port counts as closed. An inventory job re-observed only one ICMP finding per host. Full mode works because it includes that family. The UDP port set is probably ineffective for the same reason; that part is not verified.
- One product per port on the wire (`v1.Port`). The engine registers nginx under two CPEs (`nginx:nginx` and `f5:nginx`); only the first is kept. Advisory matching will want all of them.
- The job record's phase stays at "discovery" and progress at 0 for the whole run; progress only travels in the heartbeat's `current_job`.
- `vt_count` in engine health is always 0: ospd answers the daemon's `filter="id=none"` count query with 400.
- No MAC addresses are recorded: naabu's discovery output is parsed as bare IPs and the engine emits no MAC detail when its alive test is skipped.
- Cosmetic: CVSS values carry float32 noise such as 7.800000190734863, and finding names keep HTML entities such as `<`.

**Why:** these decide whether the planned advisory matching can work, because it depends on the product inventory ([[project-goal-qualys-parity]]).

**How to apply:** check whether each item is still present before repeating it. When changing how results are parsed, capture real engine output in the lab first; do not trust `daemon/internal/osp/osptest` to reflect the real wire format.
""")

# Counts what the appliance sends to the lab targets while a scan runs:
# TCP connection attempts (SYN) and UDP datagrams, per destination port.
import socket, struct, json, os, time, sys
out, stop = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
targets = {"172.18.0.4", "172.18.0.5", "172.18.0.6", "172.18.0.7"}
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_PACKET, socket.SOCK_RAW, socket.ntohs(0x0003))
s.bind(("eth0", 0)); s.settimeout(1.0)
tcp, udp = {}, {}
t0 = time.time()
while not os.path.exists(stop) and time.time() - t0 < 1800:
    try:
        pkt, addr = s.recvfrom(65535)
    except socket.timeout:
        continue
    if addr[2] != 4 or len(pkt) < 34 or pkt[12:14] != b"\x08\x00":   # outgoing IPv4 only
        continue
    ihl = (pkt[14] & 0x0F) * 4
    proto = pkt[23]
    dst = socket.inet_ntoa(pkt[30:34])
    if dst not in targets:
        continue
    l4 = 14 + ihl
    if proto == 6 and len(pkt) >= l4 + 14:
        dport, flags = struct.unpack("!H", pkt[l4 + 2:l4 + 4])[0], pkt[l4 + 13]
        if flags & 0x02 and not flags & 0x10:
            tcp[(dst, dport)] = tcp.get((dst, dport), 0) + 1
    elif proto == 17 and len(pkt) >= l4 + 4:
        dport = struct.unpack("!H", pkt[l4 + 2:l4 + 4])[0]
        udp[(dst, dport)] = udp.get((dst, dport), 0) + 1
json.dump({"tcp": [[h, p, n] for (h, p), n in tcp.items()], "udp": [[h, p, n] for (h, p), n in udp.items()]}, open(out, "w"))

# Polls the Greenbone Community Feed's version file every 15 minutes and
# exits 0 when it names a version other than the one the lab already has.
import re, subprocess, sys, time, datetime
SRC = "rsync://feed.community.greenbone.net/community/vulnerability-feed/22.04/vt-data/nasl/plugin_feed_info.inc"
DST = sys.argv[1]
HAVE = sys.argv[2]
deadline = time.time() + 4 * 3600
while time.time() < deadline:
    now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%H:%M:%S")
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["rsync", "-t", "--timeout=120", SRC, DST], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=180)
        ver = ""
        if r.returncode == 0:
            m = re.search(r'PLUGIN_SET\s*=\s*"(\d+)"', open(DST).read())
            ver = m.group(1) if m else ""
        print(now, "rsync exit", r.returncode, "version", ver or "?", flush=True)
        if ver and ver != HAVE:
            print("new feed version", ver, flush=True)
            sys.exit(0)
    except Exception as e:
        print(now, "error", e, flush=True)
    time.sleep(900)
print("gave up after 4 hours", flush=True)
sys.exit(1)
EOF

A canary that reports `update_error` holds the rollout. Releases are per platform (`applianced-<os>-<arch>`); containers are skipped because they update by image.
- **Bundles overlap.** With a bundle a day and a 48-hour canary period several bundles are in canary at once, and the newest always is. So every appliance is offered the newest bundle it may run: canary appliances take bundles in canary, all others take released ones. A canary's confirmation is recorded when it reports the bundle, because by the end of the period it runs a newer one. On 2026-10-05 the user chose "option 2": prove the update path with the real feed. Bundles built from the Community Feed (95,255 files, about 105,000 with nuclei templates, 16 MB manifest) were published to the lab control plane and applied by the lab appliance. The fixes were left uncommitted for the user, who commits themselves.

**Engine facts measured, not predicted:**
- ospd-openvas checks `plugin_feed_info.inc` every 10 s and reloads only when PLUGIN_SET on disk is numerically greater than the loaded one (`feed_is_outdated` in `ospd_openvas/daemon.py`). An older feed is never loaded. A bundle with an older feed kept the appliance in `updating` for 36 minutes before it rolled back. So bundles only move forward: a hold stops the spread and the next bundle is the way out. A true feed rollback would need a redis cache reset, which is not built.
- A version-bump reload of the full feed takes about 37 s; a bundle that changes the feed applies in 45 to 51 s.
- Greenbone publishes the Community Feed once a day around 06:00 UTC. A sync before that returns the same version.
- With nuclei v3.4.10 and templates v10.5.0 at medium severity and above, about 5,860 templates run and each web server gets about 8,800 requests, about 580 of them from 292 default-login templates.

The fake ospd now only loads newer feeds, like the real one.

- Policy for the user: default-login templates run in web checks while `docs/DEPLOY.md` says brute-force checks never run. Same tension as the SNMP community names in the UDP module.

def ask(xml, wait=60):

    s.connect(SOCK); s.sendall(xml.encode()); s.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)
    buf = b""

        except socket.timeout: break
        if not c: break

{"command":"M=/Users/richardtang/.claude/projects/-Users-richardtang-Desktop-repos-scanner-appliance/memory; cat > "$M/first-real-feed-scan-open-issues.md" <<'EOF'
---
name: first-real-feed-scan-open-issues
description: Defects the first OpenVAS scans with the real Community Feed exposed (2026-10-05), which are fixed and which are open, plus engine facts measured along the way
metadata:
  type: project
---

The first end-to-end scans with the real feed ran on 2026-10-05 in the container lab (see [[local-dev-environment]]). They work, and they exposed defects the scripted fakes could not, because the fakes encode assumptions about the engine that turned out wrong.

**Fixed on 2026-10-05, committed by the user as `48fc5cb`, `9d45c5e` and `6c1dfe8`:** product inventory parsing (host details arrive as `Log Message` results on `general/Host_Details`), slow test descriptions (one streamed `get_vts` pass from 8 misses on), inventory mode seeing no services (every scan selects the feed's "SYN Scan" test, and a scan in which the engine sees no open port fails with `engine.ErrBlind`), and UDP tests as an opt-in `udp` module with `inventory+udp` / `full+udp` scopes.

**Fixed on 2026-10-07 at the user's choice ("option 1"), left uncommitted for the user:**
- One record per host. A job's first chunk has addresses and ports only, so a host that moved got a second record; `siteIndex.absorb` in `controlplane/pkg/store/correlate.go` folds an address-only record into the host once it is identified, and `match` prefers an identified record at an address. The lab went from 8 records to 7.
- MAC for every on-link host: the daemon reads the kernel neighbor table over rtnetlink (`daemon/internal/engine/neigh.go`), accepts only entries confirmed since the job started and drops a MAC that answers for several IPs. 7 of 7 lab hosts got their real MAC. On a host without an agent the appliance's MAC now replaces the stored one.
- Every CPE: `v1.Port.CPEs` and `v1.Host.CPEs` from the engine's registry (`App` / `OS` details plus details named after the CPE that give the location).
- Job phase and progress follow the heartbeat (`Store.NoteJobProgress`, a conditional update so a late heartbeat cannot undo a status); a finished job ends in phase `finalize`.
- `vt_count`: counted in the engine's redis (`daemon/internal/osp/redis.go`), once per feed version. The lab shows 95,103.
- Scores are `double precision` (migration `0008_inventory.sql`), result names are unescaped once.
- Web add-on: the nuclei `default-login` templates run only with the `default_logins` module (`--default-logins`); their findings get family `Default login (nuclei)` and scope `web+logins`. A web phase that was skipped or cut short (a `web:` warning in the stats) resolves no web finding.

**Engine facts measured on 2026-10-07 (ospd-openvas 22.10.5):**
- `get_vts` never fills its `total` attribute, refuses any filter but `modification_time`, and ignores `details="0"`: the full listing is 170 MB and takes 36 s. Redis database 1 holds one `nvt:<oid>` key per test next to the key `nvticache`; `GVM.__GlobalDBIndex` in database 0 lists the databases in use.
- The `name` attribute of a result is escaped twice (`&lt;` on the wire); names from `get_vts` are not.
- nginx logs the user name of a Basic-auth attempt (`$remote_user`) whether or not the page needs one, so its access log counts sign-in attempts. Apache httpd and Tomcat log a user only after a successful sign-in.
- Web add-on with templates v10.5.0: about 8,150 requests per web server without the default-login set and about 610 more with it. Without it nginx still saw 35 requests with a built-in account.
- openvas runs its Default Accounts family (316 tests) in both scan configs, as PLAN §10.4 has it: 5 sign-in attempts per scan against nginx, and about 120 refused requests against a Tomcat management page that asks for a password. That scan did not report a default account planted on the Tomcat; the opt-in nuclei set did.

**Open, verified, not fixed:**
- Policy for the user: whether the engine's Default Accounts family stays on by default. `docs/DEPLOY.md` and the transparency page now state the measured numbers.
- The engine's "Ping Host" test sends one SYN to 18 well-known ports per host in every scan.
- Full mode selects the feed's Port scanners and Nmap NSE families (340 tests). Read from the feed and not run, because the lab image has no nmap: on an image with nmap those wrappers would run it outside the fingerprint pass and its sign-off.
- A host behind a router gets no MAC (no neighbor entry).
- The lab database holds one open `tomcat-default-login` finding from a fixture that has since been removed from the lab Tomcat.
- See [[update-path-real-feed-findings]] for the bundle path.

**Why:** these decide whether the planned advisory matching can work, because it depends on the product inventory ([[project-goal-qualys-parity]]).

**How to apply:** check whether each item is still present before repeating it. When changing how results are parsed or what the engine is asked to run, capture real engine output and count in the lab first; do not trust `daemon/internal/osp/osptest` or a reading of the openvas source to reflect real behavior. To learn what a check sends, count it in the target's own logs. Do not open the feed's default-credential tests or the default-login templates to read their credential lists: a response was stopped by the safety classifier on 2026-10-07 when I did that, and the target's logs gave the numbers that mattered anyway.
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
M='/Users/richardtang/.claude/projects/-Users-richardtang-Desktop-repos-scanner-appliance/memory/'
p=M+'update-path-real-feed-findings.md'; s=open(p).read()
old="- Policy for the user: default-login templates run in web checks while `docs/DEPLOY.md` says brute-force checks never run. Same tension as the SNMP community names in the UDP module.\n"
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,"- The default-login templates became opt-in on 2026-10-07 (`default_logins` module, see [[first-real-feed-scan-open-issues]]). What is left of that policy question is the engine's own Default Accounts family, which runs by default.\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
p=M+'local-dev-environment.md'; s=open(p).read()
old="\n**Why:** each of these caused a failed command or a detour during the 2026-09 sessions."
assert s.count(old)==1
add=("- When the Docker VM cannot reach Docker Hub, `dev/lab/compose build` hangs at \"resolve image config\" although the Mac itself reaches the registry (seen 2026-10-07). The lab can still run the working tree: build `applianced` and `cp-api` for linux/arm64 on the host with the dev CA copied into `daemon/internal/pki/` for the daemon build and restored after, `docker cp` each binary to `/usr/local/bin/` in its container and `docker restart` the container. The containers then differ from their images until the next image build.\n"
     "- Throwaway Postgres for the store conformance suite: `docker run -d --name pgconf -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=test -p 55433:5432 postgres:17`, then `TEST_DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres:test@localhost:55433/postgres?sslmode=disable' go test ./controlplane/pkg/store/`, then `docker stop pgconf` and `docker rm pgconf`.\n"
     "- `date` in a shell call is the only reliable clock for how long a lab job has run; I misjudged elapsed time several times on 2026-10-07.\n")
s=s.replace(old,add+old)
open(p,'w').write(s)
p=M+'MEMORY.md'; s=open(p).read()
old="- [First real-feed scans: fixed and open issues](first-real-feed-scan-open-issues.md) — inventory, slow fetch, inventory mode fixed; UDP opt-in module committed; open list includes duplicate hosts; measure the engine, don't predict it\n"
assert s.count(old)==1

old2="- [Update path with the real feed](update-path-real-feed-findings.md) — bundles and a real delta proven in the lab 2026-10-06; ospd only loads newer feeds; open: default-login policy, templates missing helper files, 27 MB a day of checksum lists\n"

name: bundle

# Daily signature bundle (PLAN §13, §17.3): mirror the Greenbone Community
# Feed, build the content-addressed bundle with the shipped scan configs and
# the filtered nuclei templates, sign it with the release key and publish it
# to the control plane, where it goes to the canary group first (PLAN §14).
#
# When it runs. Greenbone stamps a feed around 06:00 UTC and it reaches the
# rsync mirror about 4.5 hours later: at 10:48, 10:42 and 10:48 UTC on
# 2026-10-05, -06 and -07. The first run follows that; the second is for a
# day on which the feed is late. A run that finds nothing new publishes
# nothing: the control plane answers "unchanged" for a bundle whose files
# are those of the newest one, so a day without a feed (there seem to be
# none at weekends) does not send every appliance a new file list.
#
# Secrets:
#   CP_ADMIN_URL         https://cp.example.com:9443 (the mTLS listener also serves /admin)
#   CP_ADMIN_TOKEN       bearer token for /admin
#   CP_ROOT_CA_PEM       root CA the control plane's server certificate chains to (optional)
#   RELEASE_KEY_PEM      the release signing key (cp-api ca init: release-key.pem)
#   FEED_GPG_KEYRING_B64 optional: base64 GPG keyring with Greenbone's feed key, verifies sha256sums.asc
# Variables:
#   FEED_SOURCE          rsync source (default: the Community Feed 22.04 nasl module)
#   NUCLEI_TEMPLATES_REF pinned nuclei-templates commit/tag (default: the tag the lab runs were made with)

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "23 11 * * *"
    - cron: "23 15 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      canary_hours:
        description: "Canary period before general release (hours)"
        default: "48"

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: bundle
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build-and-publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
          cache: true

      - name: Preflight
        env:
          CP_ADMIN_URL: ${{ secrets.CP_ADMIN_URL }}
          RELEASE_KEY_PEM: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_KEY_PEM }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$CP_ADMIN_URL" ] || [ -z "$RELEASE_KEY_PEM" ]; then
            echo "::error::CP_ADMIN_URL and RELEASE_KEY_PEM secrets are required"
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s\n' "$RELEASE_KEY_PEM" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-key.pem"
          if [ -n "${{ secrets.CP_ROOT_CA_PEM }}" ]; then
            printf '%s\n' "${{ secrets.CP_ROOT_CA_PEM }}" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/cp-root.pem"
            echo "CP_ROOT_CA=$RUNNER_TEMP/cp-root.pem" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi
          if [ -n "${{ secrets.FEED_GPG_KEYRING_B64 }}" ]; then
            echo "${{ secrets.FEED_GPG_KEYRING_B64 }}" | base64 -d > "$RUNNER_TEMP/feed.gpg"
            echo "CP_FEED_GPG_KEYRING=$RUNNER_TEMP/feed.gpg" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          fi
          sudo apt-get update -q && sudo apt-get install -y -q rsync

      - name: Build cp-api
        run: go build -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/cp-api" ./controlplane/cmd/cp-api

      # The templates are checked with the nuclei version the appliance image
      # carries (the pin in ci/build-engine.sh): what loads depends on it.
      - name: Restore nuclei
        id: nuclei
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: engine-bin
          key: bundle-nuclei-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('ci/build-engine.sh') }}

      - name: Build nuclei (the image's version)
        if: steps.nuclei.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: ci/build-engine.sh --only nuclei --out engine-bin

      - name: Restore the feed mirror
        id: mirror
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: feed-mirror
          # Never an exact match: the newest saved mirror comes from restore-keys.
          key: feed-mirror-restore-${{ github.run_id }}
          restore-keys: |
            feed-mirror-

      - name: feed sync (rsync + sha256sums)
        id: sync
        env:
          CP_FEED_SOURCE: ${{ vars.FEED_SOURCE }}
        run: |
          args=(--dest feed-mirror)
          [ -n "$CP_FEED_SOURCE" ] && args+=(--source "$CP_FEED_SOURCE")
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/cp-api" feed sync "${args[@]}" | tee feed-sync.out
          echo "feed_version=$(tail -n 1 feed-sync.out | jq -r .feed_version)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # One saved mirror per feed version, so a run that found no new feed
      # does not store another 480 MB.
      - name: Save the feed mirror
        if: steps.sync.outputs.feed_version != '' && steps.mirror.outputs.cache-matched-key != format('feed-mirror-{0}', steps.sync.outputs.feed_version)
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: feed-mirror
          key: feed-mirror-${{ steps.sync.outputs.feed_version }}

      - name: nuclei templates (pinned)
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates
          ref: ${{ vars.NUCLEI_TEMPLATES_REF || 'v10.5.0' }}
          path: nuclei-templates

      - name: bundle build
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/cp-api" bundle build --out bundle-out --feed feed-mirror \
            --nuclei-templates nuclei-templates --nuclei engine-bin/nuclei \
            --key "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-key.pem" | tee bundle-summary.json

      - name: publish (canary first)
        env:
          CP_URL: ${{ secrets.CP_ADMIN_URL }}
          CP_ADMIN_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CP_ADMIN_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/cp-api" admin publish-bundle --dir bundle-out \
            --canary-hours "${{ github.event.inputs.canary_hours || '48' }}" | tee publish.json
          if [ "$(jq -r '.unchanged // false' publish.json)" = "true" ]; then
            echo "Nothing published: bundle $(jq -r .version publish.json) (feed $(jq -r .feed_version publish.json), $(jq -r .status publish.json)) already carries these files." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "Published bundle $(jq -r .version publish.json) with feed $(jq -r .feed_version publish.json)." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: bundle-manifest
          path: |
            bundle-out/manifest.json
            bundle-out/manifest.sig
            bundle-summary.json
            publish.json
          retention-days: 30
EOF

The update path was proven with real Community Feed bundles in the container lab on 2026-10-05/06 (user's commit `dbd871e`) and finished on 2026-10-07 at the user's request "finish the update path". What is still open is in the README under "Updates: what the lab runs left open"; read that instead of trusting a list here.

**Measured, not predicted. Reuse these:**
- ospd-openvas checks `plugin_feed_info.inc` every 10 s and loads a feed only when PLUGIN_SET is numerically greater than the loaded one. An older feed is never loaded, so bundles only move forward. A reload of the full feed takes 34 to 38 s; a bundle that changes the feed applies in 41 to 51 s.
- The engine does not read Greenbone's `sha256sums` while `nasl_no_signature_check = yes`: the lab reloaded and scanned (103 findings, as before) after a bundle removed the file.
- Community Feed timing: the feed's version stamp is near 06:00 UTC and it reaches the rsync mirror about 4 h 40 min later (10:48:59, 10:42:01 and 10:48:33 UTC on 2026-10-05, -06 and -07). `rsync -t` of `plugin_feed_info.inc` alone keeps the mirror's mtime, which is the landing time. On Sunday 2026-09-27 the newest feed was Friday's, so there may be no weekend builds. I guessed this schedule wrong twice before measuring it.
- nuclei v3.4.10 opens a template's helper file only below its own template directory ("access to helper file ... denied" otherwise). `-update-template-dir DIR` together with `-disable-update-check` makes DIR that directory and fetches nothing. The `NUCLEI_TEMPLATES_DIR` variable had no effect, even with a fresh HOME. Without `-silent` nuclei writes about 1 KB to stderr for a full run, including `Templates loaded for current scan: N` and `Found N templates with runtime error`.
- Go's HTTP server counts WriteTimeout from the request header. Over HTTP/1.1 a reply written after it is cut inside a TLS record and the client reports `tls: bad record MAC` for a request the server completed. Over HTTP/2 the stream is reset the moment the deadline passes, whatever the handler is doing.
- Web add-on with templates v10.5.0 and helper files: 5,546 templates at medium and above, about 9,660 requests per web server, 1,300 of them from the Grafana plugin check for CVE-2021-43798. Before the helper files shipped it was about 8,150.

**Testing traps that cost time on 2026-10-07:**
- Shaping the control plane container's egress with `tc` also throttles its link to Postgres and its replies to the admin CLI. A publish then takes two minutes, because it checks 105,000 digests against the database. To time an appliance download on a slow link, that is fine; do not read the slow publish as a product defect.
- A lab publish of identical files under a new version is now answered "unchanged". Change one small input, for example `--fragile-ports`, to get a new bundle without a feed change.
- A mutation that leaves a variable unused shows as CAUGHT with no failing test name: it did not compile. Reword it.
